text:
Mira (Design): Hey team — dropping the latest iteration of the routing policies editor. Focus this pass: sequencing affordances, contrast for priority chips, and how the preview simulation surfaces validation hints. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/routing-editor (frame: Sequencing+Preview). Screenshot attached.

designbot: Screenshot uploaded: img_2026-03-12_14-02.png :camera: 

Alex (PM): Nice — first glance: the priority chips read small at 1200px width. Can we try bolder text and increase tappable area? Mobile thumb targets may be tight.

Mira (Design): Good call. Thinking: make chips 40px min-height, 16px body-semibold, add a 24px drag handle hit target. Thoughts about color? Current orange on light gray doesn't meet AA for 14px.

Sam (Eng): @Mira agreed on hit targets. Implementation note: drag handle should be keyboard-focusable and support move-up/move-down keybinding. We can implement aria-grabbed and role="listitem" for screenreaders.

Jia (Research): From unmoderated tests — people didn't notice validation attachments in the preview because they were tucked into a collapsed area. We should inline the top-level validation count and expose the first error inline.

Mira (Design): Proposal: show a small red badge on the preview bar with count and on hover/focus expand the first validation. Example copy for the inline hint: "Rule 2: no match conditions — add at least one matcher to route traffic." Thoughts on phrasing?

Alex (PM): Slight tweak: "Rule 2: No match conditions specified. Add a matcher (e.g., model, route) to enable this rule." More actionable.

Sam (Eng): Agree on copy. Also watch for weird reflow when the preview expands — prefer overlay anchored to the preview bar instead of pushing the whole canvas.

Mira (Design): Noted. Also accessibility nit: focus order when you tab into the rules list should land on the first rule card and then on the drag handle. That lets keyboard users reorder without hunting for the control.

Sam (Eng): Implementation detail: we can set tabindex="0" on the drag handle and tabindex="-1" on card body, then swap on arrow moves. Will prototype.

Jia (Research): Small language note from test participants: "preview simulation" is unclear — they called it "Test run" or "Simulate rules". Suggest we A/B test label variants in the header.

Mira (Design): Good idea. I'll add copy variants: [Simulate rules], [Test run], [Preview]. Will annotate in Figma.

Alex (PM): Another UX question: ordering fallback rules. If a user drags a rule to top and it fails validation, should the preview still play it? I'd err on preventing broken rules from being active — show a disable-with-tooltip state.

Sam (Eng): Can do. Suggest rule status states: active, disabled (validation-failed), draft. Quick snippet for validation payload we'll show in preview: 
```
{
  "rule_id": "r-123",
  "status": "validation_error",
  "errors": ["no matcher specified", "timeout unset"]
}
```
Mira (Design): UI treatment: disabled rules get 50% opacity + "Fix to enable" CTA. Shall we keep the CTA inline on the card or only in the preview overlay?

Jia (Research): Inline CTA performed better in tests — users clicked it more often than reading overlay text.

Alex (PM): Copy suggestion for CTA: "Complete rule to enable routing" (short).

Mira (Design): I'll update mocks: bigger chips, accessible drag handle, inline validation count + overlay preview, improved copy variants. Leaving one open question: contrast for the priority highlight (currently orange). @Sam can you run quick WCAG check on the new hex I'll drop?

Sam (Eng): Yep — drop the hex and I’ll run the script against 14/16px sizes. Also will mock keyboard reorder behavior in the storybook component.

Mira (Design): Thanks — next steps: I’ll push updated frames, add copy variants, and tag for a small usability pass with Jia. Action owners: Mira (update Figma/mocks), Sam (prototype keyboard reorder + contrast check), Jia (quick 6-person unmoderated test on label variants). Target: sync in next design review on Tuesday. :spiral_calendar:

Alex (PM): Perfect. One more tiny copy nit: change "Add rule" primary button -> "Create rule" to avoid the ambiguous verb.

Mira (Design): Done in figma v2. Will ping when ready. :white_check_mark:
